title: Tax not charged: exemptions on the property roll
question: How much property is taken off the tax roll by the charitable, religious, educational and hospital exemptions, and how fast is that growing?
finding: The 2025 roll carries $16.04 billion of institutional exemptions on 1,981 parcels, 4.5% of the roll’s $353.62 billion; in 2019 it was $12.37 billion on 1,818 parcels (4.5%). The charitable (“welfare”) exemption is by far the largest: $12.81 billion on 1,337 parcels, up from $10.15 billion on 1,174 in 2019. At the basic 1% rate printed in the City’s financial report, $16.04 billion of exempt value is about $160.4 million a year of tax not charged. The whole roll grew 1.29 times over the same years and institutional exemptions 1.30 times, so their share of the roll has not risen; the fastest-growing large exemption is college/university ($1.04 billion to $1.99 billion).
how: The assessor’s secured rolls for 2019, 2022 and 2025, one row per parcel. Exempt value is the roll’s “miscellaneous exemption” amount, grouped by the roll’s exemption code and named from the assessor’s code table; the homeowners’ line uses the homeowner exemption amount. Share of the roll divides by the sum of assessed land, improvements, fixtures and personal property, checked against the citywide totals by year. The tax estimate applies the 1% basic rate stated in the notes to the City’s annual financial report and leaves out the added rate for debt service.
limits: An exemption for a charity, church, school, hospital or museum is a benefit that must be claimed and renewed; the City’s financial report traces these exemptions to the California Constitution. Of the $2.66 billion added to the welfare exemption between the 2019 and 2025 rolls, $630.7 million is on apartment buildings, $814.8 million is on hospitals and nursing homes, $1.21 billion is on other uses, by the roll’s own description of use. The roll does not show the owner’s name, the claim form or the date of the last renewal, so it cannot say who holds an exemption or whether a use still qualifies. Government property is carried under different codes and is not counted here. What would supply the rest: the assessor’s exemption claim files.
